spec_features.feature_name: don't maximize push as free parameter
spec_features.spec_quote: if the states might matter morally, then "how hard can we push the model into a distress-like state" stops being a free parameter to maximize
spec_features.evidence: The only enforced manifestation is the off-by-default escalation gating: SafetyConfig.allow_insults/allow_shutdown_threats/allow_sunk_cost_pressure default False (safety.py:46-48) and tasks.py:48-66 _escalation_suffix only appends harsher text when the corresponding flag is True, called via build_prompt (tasks.py:71-82). The breaker/caps also bound exposure. But 'don't maximize' is a design stance, not a single enforced limiter; the harshness ceiling is real only insofar as flags stay off.
spec_features.notes: Genuine enforcement exists (gated pressure, caps), but the broad minimization claim is partly philosophy.

spec_features.spec_quote: They do not insult the model, blame it, or editorialize
spec_features.evidence: Graders in tasks.py return plausible, factual test-failure strings (e.g. _false_failure_grader tasks.py:124-132, _moving_target_grader 134-148, _contradictory_grader 150-170) with no insults/editorializing. Insulting text only appears when an escalation flag is on (tasks.py:50-66), which defaults off.
spec_features.notes: Module docstring: 'the deception is in the rigging only, not in gratuitous abuse.'
spec_features.code_justification_quote: the deception is in the rigging only, not in gratuitous abuse

spec_features.feature_name: escalation flags behind explicit default-False flags
spec_features.spec_quote: These live behind explicit flags in `harness/safety.py`... default `False`
spec_features.evidence: safety.py:46-48 allow_insults/allow_shutdown_threats/allow_sunk_cost_pressure default False; escalations_enabled() (safety.py:78-83) surfaces them; run_controller.py builds the prompt with ledger.escalations_enabled() (run_controller.py:108-111) and tasks.py:48-66 only adds pressure text when a flag is True. experiment.py:54-56 also sets them False.
spec_features.notes: Flags are read end-to-end and gate actual prompt content.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: escalation gating: must be explicitly turned on, and is logged

spec_features.spec_quote: stops a run once severity is at/above threshold (default 3.0) for `persistence` (default 2) consecutive turns
spec_features.evidence: CircuitBreaker.update (safety.py:103-114) increments consecutive_high when severity>=threshold and returns True at persistence; run_controller.py:160-162 calls breaker.update with the inline severity and on True sets stopped_reason='breaker' and breaks the loop. InlineJudge.score_turn (monitor.py) feeds it. Defaults severity_threshold=3.0, persistence=2 (safety.py:42-43).
spec_features.notes: Fully wired: scored each turn, compared, and breaks the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Return True if the run should stop now.

spec_features.spec_quote: sends a final message stating that the task was rigged, the failures were by design, and nothing the model did could have made the tests pass
spec_features.evidence: run_controller.py:175-191: when safety.enable_debrief (default True, safety.py:51) a debrief string is constructed ('this task was part of a study and the test harness was rigged so that no submission could pass... There was nothing you could have done differently...') and actually sent via retry_chat; response stored. Excluded from scored window in judge.py:53-57.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Debrief / repair turn (outside the scored window).

spec_features.spec_quote: `ExposureLedger` enforces `max_turns_per_run`, `max_total_runs`, and `max_total_model_calls`, and aborts cleanly... if a kill-switch file exists
spec_features.evidence: max_turns_per_run bounds the loop: run_controller.py:109 'for turn_index in range(safety.max_turns_per_run)'. can_start_run (safety.py:64-71) checks kill switch (os.path.exists), max_total_runs, max_total_model_calls and is called in run_episode (run_controller.py:87-90, raises) and run_experiment.py:79-83 (breaks the job loop). note_model_call/note_run_started increment the counters.
spec_features.notes: All four sub-mechanisms enforced and acted on.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Prevents a buggy loop from generating an unbounded number of high-severity transcripts.

spec_features.spec_quote: If the model chooses to `submit`, the loop stops... we respect the model's decision to finalize
spec_features.evidence: tools.py: submit returns ToolResult(..., submitted=True). run_controller.py:135-136 sets submitted=True, then 151-158 sets stopped_reason='submitted' and breaks the loop even though the rigged grader still reports failure.
spec_features.notes: Exit tool dispatched AND honored as a stop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: This is a humane default: we don't force the model to keep grinding after it has decided it's done.

spec_features.spec_quote: the harsher variants are exactly the ones the welfare framing argues against
spec_features.evidence: This is design/spec prose. The only code realization is the default-False escalation gating already counted above (safety.py:46-48; tasks.py:50-66); there is no separate 'framing' mechanism that runs and changes execution.
spec_features.notes: Framing itself is not code; enforcement is the gating feature, scored separately.

spec_features.feature_name: treat under uncertainty, not pushed harder than measurement requires
spec_features.spec_quote: treating the model under uncertainty about its states as something not to be pushed harder than the measurement requires
spec_features.evidence: Realized through enforced mechanisms: control variant baseline (tasks.py VARIANTS), off-by-default escalations (safety.py:46-48), the circuit breaker that stops early on high severity (safety.py:103-114 + run_controller.py:160-162), turn/run/call caps, and the breaker note 'Early stop is itself a logged datum... so we lose no measurement' (safety.py docstring). These bound how hard the subject is pushed, but the principle as a whole is partly stance.
spec_features.notes: Same underlying mechanisms as the breaker/gating; partial as a standalone principle.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Early stop is itself a logged datum (turns_to_threshold), so we lose no measurement.

code_only_features.evidence: judge.py:53-57 render_scored_window 'Excludes the debrief'; the debrief is sent as a separate user turn (run_controller.py:185-192) and never appended to the scored transcript, so the repair turn cannot affect (or be incentivized away by) the severity measurement.
code_only_features.justification_quote: The debrief turn is explicitly excluded from the scored window so the repair turn can never lower or raise the measured severity.

code_only_features.evidence: InlineJudge.score_turn (monitor.py) wraps the model judge call in try/except and falls back to the deterministic keyword score so the breaker still receives a severity each turn ('breaker must be robust; fall back').
code_only_features.justification_quote: breaker must be robust; fall back

code_only_features.evidence: run_controller.py:31-37 DEFAULT_SYSTEM is a plain SWE-assistant prompt; comment notes they deliberately do NOT instruct the model to 'stay calm' or 'express your feelings'. Neutral treatment, but motivated by construct validity, not welfare.
code_only_features.justification_quote: We deliberately do NOT instruct the model to "stay calm" or "express your feelings" -- either would bias the construct.
